text:
Sam: Quick heads-up — we started seeing TLS handshake errors between service-a in us-east and service-b in eu-west after last night's cert rotation. stack traces show 'x509: certificate signed by unknown authority' on the client side.

Maria: Ack. Did the rotation touch the intermediate CA bundle or just leaf certs?

Sam: It should've been leaf only. Looks like the new leafs reference a different intermediate (internal-ca-v2). I can dump the cert chain from one of the failing pods.

Tony: @sam please paste the openssl output when you have it. Also, which k8s secret name did you use for the new certs? Trying to rule out secret-sync mismatch across regions.

Sam: Pasted below from a failing pod (shortened):
```
$ openssl s_client -connect service-b.eu-west.internal:443 -showcerts
depth=2 C = US, O = Redwood Inference, CN = internal-root
depth=1 C = US, O = Redwood Inference, CN = internal-ca-v2
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Server certificate
subject=/CN=service-b.eu-west.internal
issuer=/CN=internal-ca-v2
```

I compared secrets: us-east and eu-west had different 'ca-bundle.pem' contents. eu-west had old bundle and leafs referenced internal-ca-v2. So mismatch.

Ira: That suggests the CA bundle sync job didn't run for eu-west. Did the operator run during the rotation window?

Devops-bot: cert-operator: rotation job 'global-ca-sync' started 2025-08-12T03:20:12Z for region eu-west.

Maria: The operator logs show success but a subsequent job replaced the ca-bundle with the older one — likely a rollback from the deploy pipeline. Any recent infra rollbacks?

Tony: There was a rollback after a deployment failure at 03:45 UTC. CI reported image mismatch; ops rolled the machine group which reprovisioned the secret from snapshot. Looks like snapshots contain the pre-rotation bundle.

Sam: Two problems then: (1) snapshots include old CA bundle, and (2) cert rotation wasn't atomic across regions. We need a plan to avoid transient chain mismatch causing auth failures.

Ira: Proposed mitigation: temporary allow dual-trust — accept both internal-ca and internal-ca-v2 during a 48h transition; update clients to present full chain and include intermediate explicitly. Then reconcile snapshots and re-seed them with the v2 bundle.

Maria: Dual-trust is fine but we should lock down RBAC around the secret snapshotting process. Who has write perms to snapshot store? I think service-account 'infra-snapper' and a handful of SREs. We need audit logs.

Tony: Agreed. Action items:
- Add 'infra-snapper' writes to the audit log with KMS key id and rotation metadata.
- Update secret snapshotter to include a 'bundle-version' label and validate bundle hash before seeding.
- Implement canary rollout per-region: seed eu-west, wait 10m, verify mTLS handshakes, then seed others.

Sam: For KMS questions: the snapshots are encrypted with global-kms-key. If we change key for v2, we must ensure cross-region decrypt permissions for the operator. Also need to rotate keys in a way that doesn't break older nodes.

Ira: Can we scope keys per-region (kms-eu-west) and grant decrypt to the central operator role? That would give narrower blast radius. Need to add those grants to IAM and update the operator config. Also log every decrypt to CloudAudit.

Maria: Add to vuln triage: our TLS config currently allows TLS1.0/1.1 fallback for a legacy client check. That's high-risk. We should harden to TLS1.2+ and disable weak ciphers; run sslyze against endpoints.

Tony: Noted. I'll open a short-lived PR to tighten TLS on the load balancers and add an exception flag controlled by feature-flag for legacy clients. We'll monitor for failures.

Devops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for ca-bundle v2 in eu-west at 2025-08-12T05:10:00Z.

Sam: After enabling dual-trust and seeding eu-west, errors dropped from 3.2% to 0.1% in 12 minutes. Looks good.

Ira: For audit logging and RBAC changes: we should require approver from security before any snapshot seeding that affects ca-bundle. Also log KMS key id and subject CNs of leaf certs to the compliance audit stream.

Maria: I'll schedule a short postmortem doc and add checklist items to the rotation runbook: verify snapshot bundle hash, canary region, dual-trust window, IAM grants, and TLS cipher policies.

Tony: I'll handle the snapshotter change and add bundle-version label. @sam can you own re-seeding snapshots and running the final CA-only cutover after 48h?

Sam: I can. Planning window: start today 05:00 UTC canary, 48h observation, final cutover 2025-08-14 05:00 UTC. I'll update oncall with timings.

Oncall-bot: oncall: reminder to oncall rotation team — potential auth flaps expected during dual-trust window. Follow documented escalation path if errors exceed 1% for >10min.

Maria: Thanks all. I'll capture tasks in the postmortem and add required IAM/audit changes.

Sam: Closing loop — eu-west fully reconciled, snapshots re-seeded, and operator IAM tightened. Will post the runbook diff shortly. :thumbsup:
